items.subject: Escherichia coli O157:H7
items.caption: Dos grupos de E. coli O157:H7: sin fibras curli (izquierda) y con fibras curli (derecha). No representa necesariamente otras cepas de E. coli.
items.credit: USDA; adaptación editorial de OpenStax/Rice University
items.source_caption_original: E. coli O157:H7 causes serious foodborne illness. Curli fibers (adhesive surface fibers that are part of the extracellular matrix) help these bacteria adhere to surfaces and form biofilms. Pictured are two groups of cells, curli non-producing cells (left) and curli producing cells (right). (credit left, right: modification of work by USDA)
items.source_alt_original: Micrograph of oval cells with and without projections.
items.changes: Archivo JPEG original sin modificar, recortar, redimensionar ni retocar. Leyenda traducida al español.

items.subject: Candida albicans
items.caption: Levaduras de C. albicans. Ejemplo de una especie del género Candida; no representa todas sus especies.
items.credit: CDC; adaptación editorial de OpenStax/Rice University
items.source_caption_original: Candida albicans is a unicellular fungus, or yeast. It is the causative agent of vaginal yeast infections as well as oral thrush, a yeast infection of the mouth that commonly afflicts infants. C. albicans has a morphology similar to that of coccus bacteria; however, yeast is a eukaryotic organism (note the nuclei) and is much larger. (credit: modification of work by Centers for Disease Control and Prevention)
items.source_alt_original: A light micrograph with a clear background and blue cells. A long row of cells forms a central strand. Attached to this are clusters of many spherical cells. Each cell is approximately 5 µm in size and contains a nucleus.
items.changes: Archivo JPEG original sin modificar, recortar, redimensionar ni retocar. Leyenda traducida al español.
